lines: Description:
Create the standalone configuration and download the selected provider bridge
Usage:
init [options]
Options:

--provider=PROVIDER  AI provider to configure (any symfony/ai platform — e.g. anthropic, openai, gemini); defaults to anthropic. Instance-keyed platforms take the instance too, e.g. generic.my_gateway. Skips the prompt when set.
--model=MODEL        Model the auditor should use; defaults to claude-opus-4-8 for every provider, so set it for any other. Skips the prompt when set.
--env-var=ENV-VAR    Environment variable holding the API key; defaults to <PLATFORM>_API_KEY

--base-url=BASE-URL  Base URL of the platform endpoint, required by the platforms that declare one (albert, amazeeai, generic.<instance>, openresponses.<instance>); passing it with any other platform is rejected. Skips the prompt when set.

--endpoint=ENDPOINT  Endpoint the platform should reach, for the platforms that declare one (deepgram, elevenlabs, minimax, ollama, together, venice); passing it with any other platform is rejected. Required for ollama, which declares no default. Skips the prompt when set.

--no-api-key         Write no api_key at all, for the platforms whose key is optional (bedrock, deepgram, elevenlabs, generic, ollama, openresponses); use it for a local server that authenticates nobody
--force              Overwrite an existing configuration without asking
-h, --help               Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command
--silent             Do not output any message
-q, --quiet              Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed
-V, --version            Display this application version
--ansi|--no-ansi     Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output
-n, --no-interaction     Do not ask any interactive question
-v|vv|vvv, --verbose     Increase the verbosity of messages: 1 for normal output, 2 for more verbose output and 3 for debug
Help:
The init command writes the standalone configuration and downloads the provider bridge it needs.

Every option it does not receive is asked for. Under --no-interaction the ones with defaults fall back to them, and a platform that requires a --base-url or an --endpoint is refused rather than written half-configured.
Defaults:
--provider  anthropic
--model     claude-opus-4-8 — set it for any other provider, it is not derived from one
--env-var   <PLATFORM>_API_KEY, except for a platform you host yourself, which is written without a credential unless you name one
A platform configured per instance needs the instance in --provider, and the endpoint it reaches in --base-url:
init --provider=openai --model=gpt-5.6 --no-interaction
init --provider=generic.my_gateway --base-url=https://your-gateway.example --env-var=GATEWAY_TOKEN --model=your-model
init --provider=ollama --endpoint=http://localhost:11434 --model=llama3.2 --no-interaction

A platform spells its connection URL one way or the other, never both: --base-url for albert, amazeeai, generic and openresponses, --endpoint for deepgram, elevenlabs, minimax, ollama, together and venice. A --base-url, and the --endpoint of ollama or together, is the origin only: the bridge appends its own path, so do not include a trailing /v1. deepgram, elevenlabs, minimax and venice take the endpoint with its API version path, the way their defaults spell it (https://api.deepgram.com/v1/).
--no-api-key writes no credential at all, for the platforms whose key the bundle leaves optional. Ollama takes that route by default, since a local install authenticates nobody.
A platform whose block it cannot write (azure, cartesia, lmstudio, …) still gets its bridge installed, and the block to complete by hand is printed instead.
cache and failover, which wrap other platforms through services only a Symfony application defines, run from the bundle alone: they are refused, with neither a bridge nor a block.
